newsitem.title: UK: May coffee consumer stocks up at 10.9 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: May coffee consumer stocks up at 10.9 mln bags.

text.p: World consumer coffee stocks stood at 10.9 million bags in May, up from 9.9 million in April and 1.8 million bags higher than in May 1996, UK trade house E D & F Man said on Thursday.
Stocks in Europe rose to 7.6 million bags from 6.8 million in April and 1.8 million higher than in April last year, Man said in its June/July coffee report.
U.S. stocks rose to 1.97 million bags in May from 1.85 million in April, but were 294,000 lower than in May 1996. Stocks in Japan were also higher at 1.24 million bags, up by 319,000 yer-on-year.
Man said U.S. certified stocks had started to increase in early July as coffee has been attracted to the terminal by the 20 U.S. cents/lb premium for the July contract against September.

Roasters stopped pricing coffee against the July some time ago and have resisted increasing differentials when pricing against September, so delivering coffee against the board has become the only way of obtaining the spot premium, the trade house said.

"It is noticeable that a number of secondary mild origins have contributed a major part of the increase and significant quantities of mild coffee from the Dominican Republic, Peru, Uganda and India have found their way to the board," it added.
Man also said the increase in stocks to 10.9 million bags at end May has, however, given roasters a small comfort zone.

The increase in European mild stocks, with the amount of coffee held in Bremen/Hamburg more than doubling to 2.3 million since the beginning of the year, has also encouraged the trade to take the gamble of shipping coffee to the U.S. hoping it grades before the July expiry, the trade house said.
